plain.li: [greetings,warm,their:seers] Your letter was read in the tower under a clear glass, {WRITER}, and a clear glass is a kind sky.
[greetings,cordial,their:seers] The tower has your letter, {WRITER}, and has written down the day it came, as it writes down everything.
[greetings,cool,their:seers] We have your letter. The glass has not made up its mind about you yet.
[news,warm,their:seers] The tower watches the whole region's sky, {WRITER}, and the roads under it. Here is what the season wrote.
[news,cordial,their:seers] Our runners carry the weather from town to town, and the news with it. This is the season's.
[help,warm,their:seers] What you asked for is coming with a vial-runner, {WRITER}, and the glass says fair roads for it.
[help,cordial,their:seers] The tower can spare it, and it is on the road with our runner.
[help,refusal,their:seers] The hail took our stores this season, {WRITER}, the way it took the first reader's. We have nothing to send, and we are sorry.
[invitation,warm,their:seers] A reader will come, and read your sky for you while they stay.
[condolences,warm,their:seers] We have sealed a vial of tonight's rain for your dead, {WRITER}, and set it on the shelf with the tower's own.
[condolences,cordial,their:seers] The Conclave is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. Every storm is written down, and so is every grief.
[warning,warm,their:seers] Your warning reached the tower before the trouble did, {WRITER}, and for once the sky was not the first to tell us. We will not forget it.
[warning,cordial,their:seers] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The tower's shutters are down tonight.
[greetings,warm,their:grovekeepers] Your letter was read under the oldest tree in the grove, {WRITER}, and it listened as well as we did.
[greetings,cordial,their:grovekeepers] The grove has your letter, {WRITER}. We are slow to answer, but we remember.
[greetings,cool,their:grovekeepers] We have your letter. The forest remembers every axe, and we are still counting yours.
[news,warm,their:grovekeepers] The groves hear the region as trees do, {WRITER}, slowly and all of it. Here is what a season brought.
[news,cordial,their:grovekeepers] Seed-carriers walk every road, and listen on all of them. This is what they heard.
[help,warm,their:grovekeepers] What you asked for is coming with a leaf-runner, {WRITER}. Plant it, and be patient, as we say.
[help,cordial,their:grovekeepers] The grove can spare it, and a runner is bringing it.
[help,refusal,their:grovekeepers] The groves gave everything to the dry season, {WRITER}, and are only now putting out leaves again. We have nothing to send.
[invitation,warm,their:grovekeepers] A seed-carrier will come, with a sapling for your gate.
[condolences,warm,their:grovekeepers] We planted a sapling for your dead this morning, {WRITER}, beside our own. In the end we are all the grove.
[condolences,cordial,their:grovekeepers] The Mossborn are sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. A grave that grows is a grave that is not forgotten.
[warning,warm,their:grovekeepers] Your warning reached the grove in time, {WRITER}, and everyone is in among the old trees. The grove remembers who told it.
[warning,cordial,their:grovekeepers] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The grove will keep its fires low tonight.
[greetings,warm,their:mercenaries] Your letter was read in the hall of the Roll, {WRITER}, and the captain called it a good one, which the captain rarely does.
[greetings,cordial,their:mercenaries] The fort has your letter, {WRITER}, and has filed it with the contracts.
[greetings,cool,their:mercenaries] We have your letter. The Banner keeps its word to those who pay, and we have not settled what you are yet.
[news,warm,their:mercenaries] The company marches every road of the region in a year, {WRITER}, and hears what every town is afraid of. Here is this season's.
[news,cordial,their:mercenaries] Soldiers talk at every fire, and some of it is true. This is the part we believe.
[help,warm,their:mercenaries] What you asked for is coming with a banner-runner, {WRITER}, and nobody will bill you for it.
[help,cordial,their:mercenaries] The paymaster can spare it, and it is on the road.
[help,refusal,their:mercenaries] The company is between contracts and between meals this season, {WRITER}. There is nothing to send, and we do not promise what we cannot pay.
[invitation,warm,their:mercenaries] A sergeant will come, and look over your walls while they are there.
[condolences,warm,their:mercenaries] Your dead were read out in the hall of the Roll tonight, {WRITER}, beside our own. Every name on the Roll.
[condolences,cordial,their:mercenaries] The Banner is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. Nobody is left on the field, and nobody is forgotten.
[warning,warm,their:mercenaries] Your warning reached the fort in time, {WRITER}, and the walls were manned when it came. The Banner owes you, and it pays.
[warning,cordial,their:mercenaries] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The watch is doubled tonight.
[greetings,warm,their:artisans] Your letter was read in the guildhall, {WRITER}, and the kiln-warden said the hand was good, which is high praise from a mason.
[greetings,cordial,their:artisans] The guildhall has your letter, {WRITER}. Send us something well made one day, and we will talk properly.
[greetings,cool,their:artisans] We have your letter. We judge a people by its work, and have not seen yours.
[news,warm,their:artisans] Our journeymen live a year in every town of the region, {WRITER}, and write home about all of it. Here is the best.
[news,cordial,their:artisans] Every market has its talk, and our traders bring it back with the wares. This is the season's.
[help,warm,their:artisans] What you asked for is coming with a guild runner, {WRITER}, packed properly, the way we pack everything.
[help,cordial,their:artisans] The guild can spare it, and it is on the road.
[help,refusal,their:artisans] The kilns are cold for want of fuel this season, {WRITER}, and everything we have is going into them. There is nothing to send.
[invitation,warm,their:artisans] A journeyman will come, and leave a little guild work behind.
[condolences,warm,their:artisans] We cut your dead's name into the guildhall's lintel this morning, {WRITER}, with the guild's own. Good work outlasts us.
[condolences,cordial,their:artisans] The guild is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. We mark what we make so it is remembered, and we will remember yours.
[warning,warm,their:artisans] Your warning reached the guildhall in time, {WRITER}, and the doors are barred and the kilns banked. The guild owes you, and pays well.
[warning,cordial,their:artisans] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The guildhall's doors are shut tonight.
[arrive,their:seers] Word from the tower, and the glass was clear when I left.
[leave,their:seers] The sky is turning in the west, so I will go while it lets me.
[deliver,their:seers] From the tower, sealed like a vial.
[arrive,their:grovekeepers] Word from the grove, carried slowly and carefully.
[leave,their:grovekeepers] There is a stump on the road home that needs a seed.
[deliver,their:grovekeepers] From the grove, with its patience.
[arrive,their:mercenaries] Banner-runner, with word from the fort.
[leave,their:mercenaries] I am paid to the next fort, so I will be going.
[deliver,their:mercenaries] From the paymaster, counted twice.
[arrive,their:artisans] Word from the guildhall, and the seal is the guild's own mark.
[leave,their:artisans] The kiln is lit for tomorrow, and I should be there.
[deliver,their:artisans] From the guild, packed properly.
[arrive,their:seers] Your sky has been busy this season, I can see it.
[wait,their:seers] The glass speaks to those who wait, so I can wait.
[stay,their:seers] A good roof, and a good view of the west.
[leave,their:seers] Keep an eye on the glass, and on the west.
[pass,their:seers] What the sky has done, it will do again.
[arrive,their:grovekeepers] Good trees on the way in, you have kept some.
[wait,their:grovekeepers] A year is a short time, so an hour is nothing.
[stay,their:grovekeepers] It smells of cut wood in here, and of supper.
[leave,their:grovekeepers] Plant something before I come again, and be patient with it.
[pass,their:grovekeepers] In the end we are all the grove.
[arrive,their:mercenaries] Good walls, I would hold these.
[wait,their:mercenaries] Soldiers wait for a living, take your time.
[stay,their:mercenaries] Dry bedding and a hot supper, that is a good billet.
[leave,their:mercenaries] Paid to the day, held to the day, and good day to you.
[pass,their:mercenaries] The wall is the work, remember that.
[arrive,their:artisans] Who built that wall, because I would like a word with them.
[wait,their:artisans] I will look at your joinery while I wait.
[stay,their:artisans] Honest work in this room, I can see the marks.
[leave,their:artisans] Mark what you make, and answer for it.
[pass,their:artisans] Anyone can stack stone, so build something people will come to see.
[chat,them,their:seers] We are rarely wrong and never sure, and the second is the harder to learn.
[endwarm,them,their:seers] When the glass clouds for you, I will send a runner, I promise.
[faithtalk,them,their:seers] Hesper Lyle sealed the rain of every storm for thirty years, and the tower still keeps her shelf.
[chat,them,their:grovekeepers] Every tree you fell owes the world a seedling, and we only come to collect.
[endwarm,them,their:grovekeepers] When your time comes, I hope somebody plants you a good oak.
[faithtalk,them,their:grovekeepers] Elin Sedge planted an acorn beside every stump in her valley, and she lies under the last one still.
[chat,them,their:mercenaries] No pay, no wall, and nobody in the company pretends otherwise.
[endwarm,them,their:mercenaries] If you ever need a wall held, send for the Banner and ask for me.
[faithtalk,them,their:mercenaries] Corra Mallin sold every banner but the grey one so five hundred of us would not starve, and we read the Roll for her still.
[chat,them,their:artisans] Bad work is a lie told in stone, and we tell the truth for a living.
[endwarm,them,their:artisans] Make something good while I am gone, and I will come back to look at it.
[faithtalk,them,their:artisans] Oswin Kell built the Hardwater bridge four times and marked every stone, and the fourth still stands.
Held the wall, and is written so.
Every name on the Roll, and this one with them.
Nobody is left on the field.
Read it again, so everyone hears it.
They stood where it was hardest, and that is what the Roll is for.
I keep thinking they'll come in off the wall for supper.
Paid to the day, held to the day, and then some.

gloomy.li: A name in a book is not the same as them here.

warm.li: They would have hated the fuss, and loved the book.

plain.li: [opt0] A keeper of the Ashen Banner read {DEAD}'s name into the Roll at the grave tonight, with all of us there. It is in their book now, beside soldiers from a war nobody remembers.
[opt1] I stood at {DEAD}'s grave with the keeper of the Roll. The keeper read the name once, quietly, to me.
[opt2] The Banner wanted {DEAD}'s name for their Roll and we said no. {DEAD} was ours, not theirs.

gloomy.li: [opt0] A name read out, and then a book closed.
